segment.source: Profile: {value}.
Failed sign-ins are not slowed down.

notes.note: Explains the numbers below in the lockout editor.

segment.source: An account gets the attempts below from one network (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64), then the waits in order and, in the modes that lock, a lock that ends by itself. Across all networks the account gets a delay of at most the ceiling below once it fails as often as one network may, and administrators get an alarm. The last administrator is never locked by the network. A passkey passes the lock unless the setting below holds it.
Attempts from one network
1 to 20 tries before the first wait.
Enter a whole number from 1 to 20.
Waits after the attempts
Seconds, separated by commas, in order: 1 to 10 values, each from 1 to 86400.
Enter 1 to 10 whole numbers of seconds, each from 1 to 86400, separated by commas.
Lock period
From 1 minute to 1 day. The lock always ends by itself.
Enter a duration from 1 minute to 1 day.
Account-wide delay ceiling (seconds)
0 to 600; 0 switches the account-wide delay off.
Enter a whole number from 0 to 600.
The lock also holds for a passkey
Off: a passkey, which cannot be guessed, signs in through the lock.
Use the profile's values

segment.source: Unconfirmed PINs

A PIN stored before the PIN minimum rose to six digits stops working this many days after the upgrade unless a sign-in confirms that it is long enough. An administrator then resets it. For the last administrator, run the command tenko user unlock with the account name on the host.
Days an unconfirmed PIN keeps working
1 to 365 days. The default is {days}.
Enter a whole number of days from 1 to 365.
Use {days} days
Saved the period of unconfirmed PINs

segment.source: Zone transfers
Networks of the site (zone transfers)

Under the Hardened profile, a zone transfer to an address outside these networks needs TLS (XoT). An empty list means every transfer needs XoT. The default is the private, shared, unique-local, loopback and link-local ranges.
"{line}" is not a network in CIDR notation, such as 192.0.2.0/24 or 2001:db8::/32.
